_experiment.description: Data-driven omega: sample the Monte Carlo set Omega from the actual training data distribution (real MNIST pixels) instead of the uniform distribution U([0,255]^196). The thesis claims data-free operation as a key advantage (sec:discussion). If the sparsity curve is meaningfully better with real data, the data-free claim requires qualification. If similar, the claim is strongly supported. NOTE: requires code change — add omega_source field handling to make_omega() in sparsifier.py to sample from x_train when omega_source='data'.
literature: Lazarevich et al. 2021 (layer-wise calibration): uses a small unlabelled calibration set to reconstruct each layer — the direct data-using baseline this experiment compares against
Thesis sec:discussion: explicitly claims data-free operation as a strength — this experiment is the empirical test of that claim
